Tides are the regular rise and fall of sea levels caused mainly by the gravitational pull of the Moon, and to a lesser extent the Sun, on Earth's oceans. As the Moon orbits, its gravity creates two bulges of water — one facing the Moon and one opposite. Earth's rotation carries coastlines through these bulges, producing roughly two high and two low tides each day. Coastal geography, water depth, and weather can alter their timing and height considerably.
